materials.name: Merck & Co.
materials.why: Its 2019 npj Microgravity study of pembrolizumab crystalline suspensions is the published result our protein pillar starts from.
materials.ask: Matched ground-control recipes and viscosity methods, so a flight batch is compared with the strongest Earth process.

materials.name: JAXA
materials.why: Kibo's protein-crystallization programme is one of the largest sources of space-grown structures deposited in the PDB.
materials.ask: Growth logs and paired ground data for the proteins already in the archive, so effects can be estimated per protein.

materials.name: ESA
materials.why: ESA's APCF and PCDF protein-crystallization facilities are named in 12 of the 67 space-grown PDB entries we found.
materials.ask: Access to flight logs and the Earth controls behind those structures.

materials.name: Varda Space Industries
materials.why: Recovered orbit-grown ritonavir Form III, so small-molecule solid forms can come back from orbit.
materials.ask: Return-environment data and solid-form analytics after re-entry.

materials.name: Redwire
materials.why: Flies pharmaceutical crystallization hardware (PIL-BOX) on the ISS for biopharma customers.
materials.ask: Cartridge interface lessons and historical batch outcomes.

materials.name: RCSB PDB / wwPDB
materials.why: The archive we mined. Crystallization environment is free text today, so space-grown entries are hard to find.
materials.ask: A structured, searchable "growth environment" field for microgravity depositions.

materials.name: Cambridge Crystallographic Data Centre
materials.why: The CSD is the reference archive for drug crystal forms; our open COD analysis is a proxy for it.
materials.ask: Polymorph statistics for approved drugs to size the solid-form opportunity.

materials.name: EnergyX
materials.why: Builds lithium-extraction membranes from MOF research, the application our MOF pillar targets.
materials.ask: Selectivity and flux targets that an orbit-grown membrane would have to beat.

materials.name: Stanford XLab
materials.why: Academic group investigating MOF growth in orbit; our MOF dossier cites its work.
materials.ask: Shared growth protocols and ground controls.

foundry.name: SpaceX
foundry.why: Transporter/Bandwagon rideshares are the most frequent route to orbit for small spacecraft, and Dragon is the main US route back for pressurised cargo.
foundry.ask: A rideshare integration path, downmass on Dragon cargo returns, Starlink laser backhaul for foundry telemetry, and our ephemeris on the Starlink space-safety platform.

foundry.name: SpaceXAI (xAI / Grok)
foundry.why: Structured outputs and tool calling fit our paper → evidence record → experiment pipeline. Grok Bot fits team planning.
foundry.ask: Grok for Startups credits; Grok-in-the-loop review of every evidence record, with physical control kept in deterministic, tested logic.

foundry.name: NASA Glenn · PIMS
foundry.why: The Principal Investigator Microgravity Services characterise ISS acceleration with SAMS/MAMS; quiet growth depends on that discipline.
foundry.ask: Measurement methods and requirement curves for a free-flying foundry.

foundry.name: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics
foundry.why: Hosts public ISS physical-science data (DECLIC-DSI, OASIS, PK-4) that we inventoried and analysed.
foundry.ask: Access to the full PSI catalogue, including colloid (ACE) and crystallization runs.

foundry.name: Nvidia
foundry.why: A single solidification experiment produces image volumes that favour onboard measurement over raw downlink.
foundry.ask: Radiation-tolerant edge inference for in-situ crystal metrology.

foundry.name: LeoLabs
foundry.why: The orbit we choose sits in shells whose crowding we measured; independent conjunction screening is part of operating responsibly.
foundry.ask: Conjunction screening for candidate foundry orbits.

network.name: SpaceX
network.why: Its launch cadence and Starlink production show how reusable transport and serial manufacturing change what a fleet can cost.
network.ask: Capacity planning for a multi-foundry campaign, and Starship as a future route for larger, returnable foundry modules.

network.name: Varda Space Industries
network.why: Repeated autonomous returns are the missing link between orbital production and Earth customers.
network.ask: Return cadence and capsule capacity data to calibrate our fleet model.

network.name: Sierra Space
network.why: Dream Chaser's gentle runway landing matters for fragile, temperature-sensitive products.
network.ask: Downmass environment specifications for crystal suspensions and membranes.

network.name: ISS National Laboratory
network.why: It allocates in-space production research and connects biopharma users with flight hardware.
network.ask: A sponsored campaign to run matched flight/ground batches across two of our five materials.

network.name: Axiom Space · Vast
network.why: Post-ISS commercial stations decide where crewed research capacity will exist after 2030.
network.ask: Hosted-payload interfaces for foundry cartridges during the transition from the ISS.

network.name: Merck & Co.
network.why: The shift of biologics to subcutaneous delivery is the demand our protein pillar serves.
network.ask: Volume, specification and acceptance criteria for a first commercial batch.
